approach: Count the rejected, failed or timed-out jobs in one retry lineage (a chain of "try again on <job>" requests) from the job records. Build the count on `job_history` and `retries_by_job` in `crates/athena-core/src/reading/retry.rs`, with a named constant `LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT = 3`. A new `lineage_stop` returns, for a lineage at the limit, the failed job ids, the findings that appeared in at least two attempts, a ready-to-queue narrower request, and any narrower request already queued for that lineage. The drain asks this through two new `Steps` methods, each with a default so existing stubs compile. `Drain::attempts` checks before every attempt that is not a landing retry. At the limit it dispatches nothing (no read, no run), queues the narrower request once through the existing `Athena::queue` (channel `cli`, already drained), and ends the item with a new `ItemEnd::LineageStopped` that is passed over with the reason. The request text is built with `StewardRequest::new`, so `athena plan` accepts it. It starts with a title, not "try again on", so it begins a new lineage. It carries a marker line naming the lineage root, which also makes queuing idempotent. Add a `lineage-limit` entry to `defaults.toml`. The reader's always-loaded set is at 1997 of 2000 tokens and `docs/system-facts.md` (not a listed deliverable) records that exact size, so this revision keeps the computed reader size at exactly 1997 and leaves that file untouched: the new line's cost is offset by splitting the long first sentences of existing entries with `. ` (full statements are unchanged, only what `render()` shows is shorter), and the new entry's first-sentence wording is tuned by a few bytes until the budgets test passes. Document the limit in the drain module doc and `docs/design/async-drain.md`, and add a CHANGELOG entry. Tests: unit tests on in-memory `Records` in `reading.rs`, and a real-steps drain test showing the 4th attempt is not dispatched. Root cause: nothing counted attempts across a lineage. The drain's two attempts per item and the scope guard's T1 flag at attempt 3 (which only flags and still dispatches) both reset or stop short per run, so lineages kept growing until the operator intervened.

decisions.choice: Enforce the limit in `Drain::attempts` (crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs ~1867), before `run_job` and so before any `Steps::read` or `Steps::run`. Add to `Steps` `lineage_stop(&self, job) -> Option<LineageStop>` (default None) and `queue_narrower(&self, &LineageStop) -> Result<String, String>` (default Err). `RealSteps` implements both from `self.records()` and `self.athena.queue`.
decisions.reason: That point is where both ways of dispatching a further attempt pass: the in-item retry `ReadOf::Retry(last_job)` and a queued "try again on <job>" request (`ReadOf::Queued`) whose chain already holds 3 failures. Default methods keep every existing `Steps` implementor (tests/drain.rs `Stub` at 127, the unit-test stubs in drain.rs at 4655, 4722, 4849, 5980, 6903) compiling and behaving as before. The gate runs only when `passed.is_none()`, so a landing retry of a passed job is not a new attempt.

rejected.why: It would also block the operator's own `athena retry`, which is the manual override. The drain would see an error, not a stop, and could not queue the replacement.

rejected.option: Raise the scope guard's T1 (flag at attempt 3, `scope_guard.rs:42`) to a pause
rejected.why: A pause refuses work but queues no narrower request and records no repeated findings. T1 also groups by line and counts differently from a retry chain. `thrash-stop` text is out of scope.

rejected.option: Count attempts in the drain's own `failures` counter or raise `ATTEMPTS`
rejected.why: `failures` is per item per run; a lineage spans runs and manual retries. The two-attempt per-item rule is explicitly out of scope.

decisions.choice: Count lineage attempts from job records: go forward from the given job along `retries_by_job` to the newest standing retry, then back along `job_history`'s `retry_of` links, with a seen-set and the `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` bound each way. Count jobs whose `state()` is Closed(Rejected | Failed | TimedOut). The limit is `pub const LINEAGE_ATTEMPT_LIMIT: usize = 3` in retry.rs.
decisions.reason: It reuses the one place the "try again on" form is read (`retried_job`), counts manual and drain retries alike, and is measured on job records, not a stand-in. `retries_by_job` already skips unrun retries (dropped, declined, abandoned, stale, closed), which are not failed attempts. TimedOut is counted because `athena retry` and `RunStep::Failed.retry` treat it like rejected or failed, so a timed-out loop would otherwise stay unbounded. `job_history` maps Stale to Failed, so state is read from the record directly to keep stale out.

rejected.why: It does not use the helpers the brief names. It would also miss a retry the operator already made of the job the drain holds.

rejected.option: A new `[retry] max_attempts` key in athena.toml

decisions.choice: The replacement is an ordinary request built by `StewardRequest::new` (title, body naming the lineage root and failed attempts and the repeated findings, acceptance bullets, `Files:` from the root request's touched paths via `request_text_touches`) and queued with `Athena::queue`. The marker line is `Lineage <root job id>: ...`. `lineage_stop` finds an existing request containing that marker, so later passes queue nothing new. A finding is repeated when the same blocker or major finding (summary + location) or the same unmet criterion appears in at least 2 failed attempts. If none repeats, the body says so and lists the last attempt's findings.
decisions.reason: `StewardRequest::new` checks the text against the parse `athena plan` uses, so the drain's planning pass never refuses it for missing acceptance. `Athena::queue` redacts the text and commits a Request record on channel `cli`, which `steward::DRAINED_CHANNELS` already works. No new record type, so `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord` are untouched. Because the text does not start with "try again on", `retry_reference` gives it no parent and it starts a fresh lineage with zero attempts. The marker is an exact substring of text Athena itself generates, not a parse of operator input, so it adds no new input form to the refusal corpus.

risks.risk: Adding a default pushes the reader set (1997 of 2000 tokens) over its budget, or moves it off 1997 so `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` fails against the unedited docs/system-facts.md.
risks.mitigation: Step 8 splits `buy-first` (and, if needed, `verified` and `lazy-requests`) at `; ` into `. ` and gives the new entry a short first sentence, then tunes that sentence's wording by a few bytes. The size is ceil(bytes/3), so a 3-byte window lands on 1997; `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` prints the computed size on a mismatch, so the producer iterates until it passes. Do not change the budget. If 1997 cannot be reached, stop and report it (open question) instead of editing the facts file.

risks.risk: The test's rejecting verdict (all criteria met, one major finding) might not close the job as rejected, or the scope guard might pause the line (T4) so the drain would stop for the wrong reason.
risks.mitigation: The test asserts j1, j2 and j3 are each in `JobState::Closed(OutcomeState::Rejected)` and that `steps.paused` is empty before it asserts the lineage stop. If the judge does not reject on a finding alone, switch to a reading with three content criteria and verdicts that leave a different criterion unmet in each attempt, while keeping the same major finding in each so it repeats. Keep the assertions.

risks.risk: The drain's queue is read again after each item, so the narrower request is worked in the same run and adds jobs to the report; counting jobs naively would then look like extra attempts.
risks.mitigation: Tests assert on the lineage (`lineage_attempts`, request text `try again on <j3>`) and the marker count, not on the report's job total. The narrower request starts its own lineage at zero attempts, so it can fail twice without tripping the limit.

risks.risk: A queued "try again" item that hits the limit stays queued and is passed over every run.
risks.mitigation: `lineage_stop` finds the existing marker request, so nothing new is queued, and the pass-over line names the narrower request and says the operator may drop the item. Documented in the drain doc.

risks.risk: Findings texts could hold secrets or banned words; `Athena::queue` redacts and `refuse_banned_input` can refuse.
risks.mitigation: `StewardRequest::new` rewords boundary words. The text goes through `queue`'s redactor. If queuing still errors, the drain stops the lineage anyway and notes the error, with no 4th dispatch.

risks.risk: Depth bound: a lineage longer than `MAX_RETRY_DEPTH` (16) or with a cycle.
risks.mitigation: The walks use a seen-set and the same depth bound as `earlier_jobs`. A unit test covers a cyclic request. Past 16 hops the count is still at least 3, so the stop holds.

demonstrations.method: Same fixture and run as criterion 3, in sibling test `the_lineage_stop_queues_one_narrower_request_that_carries_the_repeated_findings`. After the drain, load `Records` and select the requests whose text contains the marker `Lineage <j1>`. Assert exactly one; its channel is `cli`; its text does not start with "try again on"; it contains `the description lists no callers` (the finding that repeated in j1, j2 and j3), the three failed job ids and acceptance bullets; and the drain report lists it as worked in place of the retry. Then call `steps.lineage_stop(j3)` and `steps.queue_narrower(&stop)` on the production `RealSteps` and assert it returns the same job id and `fx.head()` is unchanged (no second request). Also assert `athena_core::reading::request_text_acceptance(&text)` is non-empty (a plan-ready request). Core unit tests in reading.rs also cover the repeated-finding selection on in-memory records: a finding in 2 of 3 attempts is listed, one in 1 is not, and the 'none repeated' wording.
demonstrations.observes: One narrower request exists with the repeated finding text. A second queue call adds no record.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without queuing, no request carries the marker and the count of 1 fails. Without the marker check, the second call writes a second request and the unchanged-head assertion fails. If the finding were not carried, the text assertion fails.
demonstrations.seam: `RealSteps::queue_narrower` and `RealSteps::lineage_stop` (added by plan steps 4 and 5) over a real `Athena` and fixture repository (exists); the stop and request text come from `athena_core::reading::lineage_stop` (plan step 2) from the fixture's records. No double holds any of the logic; the fake agent only plays the rejecting verifier.

demonstrations.method: Read the diff of the three documentation files. The verifier checks that CHANGELOG.md has an Unreleased/Added entry naming the 3-attempt limit, the root cause and the tests; that the drain.rs module doc has a bullet on the lineage limit and the narrower request; and that async-drain.md section 10's table has a row for it. Each says the limit is enforced in the drain and that a hand `athena retry` is not limited.
demonstrations.observes: The three files contain the entries described, and each states the limit of 3, the narrower request and the manual override.

demonstrations.method: Run the whole suite, which includes the unchanged tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/retry.rs and drain.rs (every drain scenario with fewer than 3 failed attempts: the default `Stub` returns `lineage_stop` None, and the real-steps tests have at most 2 failures per lineage), plus the new tests/retry.rs test that a hand retry past 3 still reads. The refusal-corpus test (`cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus`) is run as a regression for the shared retry reading; its cases were not read and no result is claimed.
demonstrations.observes: All tests pass, and no existing test was edited: `git diff` of the test files shows only added tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the gate fired below 3 failures, `a_rejected_job_can_be_retried_twice` (tests/retry.rs:1175) and the drain tests that retry once would fail. If the gate fired on a first-attempt item, tests that expect a second attempt would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Existing tests with their existing fakes, through the production entry points `Athena::retry` and `drain::drain`. The new tests/retry.rs test uses that file's `reject_then_ask_again` and `run_retry` helpers (lines 708 and 725, names read; bodies not read). It is added in step 10.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs, each as its own whole command, in this order: `cargo fmt --all --check`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, then `cargo test --locked`. The workspace is the seam; the entry point is cargo over the whole workspace, which compiles the new `Steps` methods, the new `ItemEnd::LineageStopped` arm in `Drain::finish` and all the new tests.
demonstrations.observes: Each of the three commands exits 0: formatting is clean, clippy reports no warning (including no missed `ItemEnd` arm or unused item), and every test passes, including the new lineage tests and the budgets and defaults tests.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the change as planned: code left unformatted fails `cargo fmt --all --check`; a missed `ItemEnd::LineageStopped` arm or an unused new item fails `cargo clippy ... -D warnings`; and a missing gate in `Drain::attempts`, a missing marker check, or a reader set that no longer equals the recorded 1997 fails `cargo test --locked` (tests a_lineage_with_three_rejected_attempts_gets_no_fourth_attempt, the_lineage_stop_queues_one_narrower_request_that_carries_the_repeated_findings, system_facts_budgets_match_computed).
demonstrations.seam: Cargo workspace checks over the whole repository (exists: the commands Athena runs, listed in the brief). No fake or fixture; nothing is injected. The tests that give the run its content are added by plan steps 3, 9 and 10.

demonstrations.method: List the changed files. No path under records/ appears. The only governance file changed is defaults.toml. The other paths are the seven other deliverables (retry.rs, reading.rs, drain.rs, tests/drain.rs, tests/retry.rs, CHANGELOG.md, async-drain.md). docs/system-facts.md is not changed because the reader size is held at 1997.
demonstrations.observes: Eight paths, none under records/, and docs/system-facts.md absent from the list.

open_questions: User: should a hand-run `athena retry` also stop at 3 failed attempts? The plan limits only the drain and keeps the manual command as the operator's override, because the request says Athena should stop retrying.
User: is timed-out counted as a failed attempt acceptable? The request says "rejected or failed"; the plan also counts timed-out, since `athena retry` and the drain treat the three alike.

User: only if the reader size cannot be held at exactly 1997 tokens by splitting existing first sentences and tuning the new line, may the producer edit the `budget reader` line in docs/system-facts.md (not a listed deliverable)? The plan assumes it can be held and does not edit that file.
